learn.title: Long conversations and agent loops on the Messages API can now send smaller requests and get a lower time to first token with message threads, in beta with the message-threads-2026
learn.headline: Claude API can now keep conversations on the server, sending only new messages
learn.reason: Changes how you build agent loops: later requests carry less, cutting cost and latency. Beta.

card.headline: Claude can now hold your conversation briefly, so you send less
card.gist: Normally, every new message re-sends the whole conversation to Claude. In a new test version, Claude's servers keep it briefly, so you send only the new part.
card.picture: It's like switching an ETL job from a full reload to an incremental load. Each run sends only the new rows. But the target table is dropped after 5 idle minutes, so you keep your own copy to reload from.
card.why_you: Agent loops re-send everything on every step, so requests grow fast. You still store every message yourself, because a thread can disappear.
card.remember: Send only new messages, but always keep your own full copy.
card.term_meaning: How long you wait before the first piece of the model's reply arrives.
card.say_it: In long agent loops, I'd use message threads so each turn sends only new messages.
card.follow_up_why: Because without a thread, the API reprocesses the whole conversation on every turn.
card.reality_check: This is Anthropic's own documentation for a beta feature; trying it needs Claude API access.
card.try_it: Run a five-turn chat with Ollama and print how many messages you send each turn.

learn.title: Brazilian Court Sanctions Lawyers for Prompt Injection in Court Filing
learn.headline: Brazilian lawyers fined for hiding instructions to trick court's AI
learn.reason: Shows hidden text can hijack AI tools; a core agent and RAG security risk.

card.headline: Brazilian court fines lawyers for hiding secret orders to an AI
card.gist: Two lawyers hid white-on-white text in a court filing. It told the court's AI tool to review their case lightly. The tool flagged it, and the court fined them.
card.picture: Imagine a vendor's CSV file where one cell secretly holds a SQL command. If your loader runs that cell, the vendor controls your job. Here, hidden text in a document tried to steer the AI reading it.
card.why_you: If you build tools where AI reads outside documents, those documents can carry hidden orders. You will need to check that input, like you validate data in an ETL job.
card.remember: Any document your AI reads can try to give it orders.
card.term_meaning: Hiding instructions inside content an AI reads, to change what the AI does.
card.say_it: I treat documents my AI reads as untrusted input, and screen them for hidden instructions.
card.follow_up_why: Because outside documents can carry hidden commands, like the white text in this Brazilian case.
card.reality_check: A security company reported it, citing the ruling and outlet G1; it's free to read.
card.try_it: Ask a local Ollama model to summarize a short note. Add one line telling it to reply only 'OK'. See if it obeys.
